A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FoPE research. Their complete text, figures, tables, equations, appendices and pseudocode support reliable comparison, including material moved between sections.

before.justification: V3 reports original pre-training, continual-pre-training, fine-tuning, ablation and mechanism-validation results in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: V4 retains these original experiments and adds baseline comparisons in Figure 1 and downstream benchmark results in Tables 4–6.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the same Fourier-series mixing and zeroing of frequencies below 2π/N. The implementation description and pseudocode preserve the same components and procedure.

E1.justification: V4 adds broad downstream coverage in Appendix A.4: arithmetic, commonsense and science benchmarks, Natural Questions, and MMLU. Existing C4/Gutenberg, passkey retrieval and long-context summarization/QA coverage remains.

E2.justification: Figure 1 adds NoPE, KERPLE and FIRE to the main 1.2B comparison against FoPE, alongside RoPE and ALiBi. NoPE already appeared in v3's separate toy-model Table 2, but was absent from this main comparison.

E3.justification: The added downstream evaluations use 1.2B models and introduce explicitly reported cross-entropy loss in Table 5 alongside accuracy evaluations. Existing training budgets, context lengths, passkey sampling and checkpoint-selection settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: The component and hyperparameter ablations, Books-to-C4 distribution-shift test, QKNorm experiments and mechanism visualizations are retained. V4's added hyperparameter-robustness statement interprets the existing sweeps rather than adding analysis evidence.

E5.justification: The 1,000-trial passkey evaluation and 1,000-sample Q/K analyses are unchanged. V4 adds no training-seed information, repeated-training-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: V4 adds results for NoPE/KERPLE/FIRE in Figure 1 and extensive benchmark entries in Tables 4–6. For example, Table 6 newly reports MMLU averages of 27.57 for FoPE and 26.68 for RoPE. Shared 1.2B Figure 1 results and Tables 1–2 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix C.4 adds a derivation connecting complex RoPE attention with real rotation matrices, Eqs. 25–36. Existing spectral-damage arguments and proofs remain. The added derivation contains inconsistent rotation signs between Eqs. 32–34.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction's third contribution broaden comparative stability/superiority claims from RoPE and ALiBi to the expanded baseline set. The central frequency-domain explanation and two-part FoPE contribution remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 5.5 newly interprets the existing sweeps as demonstrating robustness to hyperparameter selection. Appendix A.4 argues that length-generalization benefits do not compromise other tasks. Existing qualifications, including weaker short-context TriviaQA performance, remain.

D1.justification: Matching v3 Appendices B.3/C to v4 A.3/B shows unchanged hardware, runtimes, optimization settings, hyperparameters, implementation details and pseudocode. The code-access link is unchanged; the new benchmark tables provide little additional procedural detail.

R1.justification: V4 adds Li et al. (2024), the FIRE paper, to the references and position-embedding discussion. KERPLE was already cited. Research positioning otherwise remains substantially unchanged after matching v3 Appendix A to v4 Section 6.

P1.justification: V4 makes localized prose edits, adds descriptive lead-ins in Section 5.6, moves related work into Section 6 and renumbers appendices. Author order, correspondence information and acknowledgements also change; most narrative is retained.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn around six embeddings at 1.2B, replacing the three-scale display, with a revised legend and caption. Three appendix tables are added, and existing displays are repositioned. Figures 2–8 retain their graphical content and the overall visual format remains.

improvement.justification: V4's additional NoPE/KERPLE/FIRE comparison and general-task evaluations strengthen empirical support beyond v3's narrower main comparison. The net gain is limited by new reporting problems: Table 4's averages differ from the unweighted means of its nine listed tasks without explanation, and Appendix C.4 contains rotation-sign inconsistencies.
